output.subject: Your question about rate locks while house hunting
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for getting in touch with us, and congratulations on starting your house hunt.

You asked whether we offer rate locks on purchase loans before you have an accepted offer on a home. You mentioned that rates keep moving while you search, and we understand why you would want some certainty before you commit to a property. It is a sensible question to ask early in the process.

We have passed your question to our Mortgage Servicing team so that the answer you receive is accurate and reflects your situation. They will respond within 10 business days with the information you asked for. If anything changes in the meantime, for example if you have an offer accepted, please let us know by replying to this message so the team has the latest picture.

Thank you again for considering us for your mortgage, and we wish you the best of luck finding the right home.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: This is a product question, not a complaint. The draft deliberately gives no answer about rate lock availability, so add the actual policy if you can answer it now.
Confirm Mortgage Servicing is the right team, since this is a new purchase loan inquiry rather than an existing loan. Mortgage origination or lending may own it instead.
The customer is actively house hunting while rates move, so a 10-business-day wait may not serve them. Consider answering directly or arranging a quicker callback from a loan officer.
If pre-offer locks or alternatives such as pre-approval exist, decide whether to mention terms, fees or eligibility. None of these are in the draft.
